title: Docker Registries — Push, Pull, Tags, Multi-arch Manifests
subtitle: How images are stored, versioned, distributed, and verified across environments

nodes.label:
docker build
Creates image layers
Content-addressed SHA256

docker push
Uploads new layers only
Sends manifest to registry

Container Registry
Docker Hub / GHCR / ECR
Stores manifests + layer blobs

panels.title: Tagging and pushing to multiple registries
panels.body:
# Build once, tag for multiple registries
docker build -t myapp:v1.2.3 .
docker tag myapp:v1.2.3 ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:v1.2.3
docker tag myapp:v1.2.3 123456.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/myapp:v1.2.3

# Push to GHCR
echo $GITHUB_TOKEN | docker login ghcr.io -u $GITHUB_USER --password-stdin
docker push ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:v1.2.3

# Push to ECR (authenticate first)
aws ecr get-login-password | docker login --username AWS \
  --password-stdin 123456.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
docker push 123456.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/myapp:v1.2.3

panels.title: Multi-arch manifest — build for amd64 + arm64 in one push
panels.body:
docker buildx create --name multi --use
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  -t ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:v1.2.3 \
  --push .

What gets pushed:
  Image index (multi-arch manifest) → references:
    linux/amd64 manifest → layers for amd64
    linux/arm64 manifest → layers for arm64

docker pull on an M2 Mac → pulls arm64 layers automatically
docker pull on CI (amd64) → pulls amd64 layers automatically

panels.title: latest tag vs immutable tags
pros: Immutable tag (v1.2.3 or SHA): reproducible builds, easy rollback, audit trail for security
SHA digest pinning (image@sha256:abc): cryptographically guaranteed — tag can be overwritten, digest cannot
cons: latest tag: convenient for dev; dangerous in production — silent image changes on next pull break reproducibility
SHA pinning: verbose in Dockerfiles; requires automation to update dependencies (Renovate, Dependabot)
